q: 'The bus is cheaper than a taxi' =
why: 보다 goes on the thing you compare against.
제일 = the most.
더 = more.
Vowel stem + ㄴ, in front of the noun.
있다 words take 는.
ㅂ stem: 맵다 → 매운.
-지만 = but.

q: 'I was busy, so I didn't go' =
why: -아/어서 never takes the past.
Stem + 고 = and.
가요 → 가 + 야 해요.
먹어요 → 먹어 + 야 해요.
안 … 도 돼요 = it's okay not to.
Stem + 고 싶어요.
좋아해요 is an action verb → 을/를.
먹 + 고 싶어요.
뭐 = what; it sits where the answer goes.
어디 = where; 에 있어요 = is at.
누구 + 가 → 누가.
ㅂ before ㄴ softens to ㅁ.
The final ㄱ slides into the empty ㅇ seat.
ㅎ between vowels goes silent.
Consonant stem + 을 거예요.

q: 'What will you do on the weekend?' =
why: 하 + ㄹ 거예요 → 할 거예요.
안 goes before the verb.
가요 → drop 요 → 갔어요.
Consonant ending → 이었어요.
해요 → 했어요; the time word goes first.
Last vowel is ㅓ (not ㅏ/ㅗ) → 어요.
ㅗ stem + 아요; 보 + 아 merge into 봐.
Same 요-form; only the tone rises.
저 ends in a vowel → 는; 학생 ends in a consonant → 이에요.
이 = this, 그 = that (near you), 저 = over there.
이름 ends in a consonant → 은; 민수 ends in a vowel → 예요.
Being somewhere → place + 에 + 있어요.
Having = 'a cat exists': 이/가 + 있어요.
없어요 = there isn't / don't have; 시간 ends in a consonant → 이.
The verb always closes the sentence.
한국어 ends in a vowel → 를; verb last.
Describing verbs take 이/가, not 을/를.
Destination with 가요 → 에.
Where an action happens → 에서.
있어요 takes 에, not 에서.
With noun + 하다, 안 goes before 해요.
Nouns are negated with 이/가 아니에요.
The negative of 있어요 is 없어요.
도 replaces 은/는 — it never stacks on it.
만 = only; it replaces 을/를.
에서 stays; 도 goes after it.
못 = can't; 안 = choose not to.
Consonant stem + 을 수 있어요 = can.

q: Asked something you're unsure about, the soft answer is:
why: 모르겠어요 is the softer 'I'm not sure'.
Drop 다 to get the stem.
좋아요 already includes 'is'.
있어요 = exist / have.
Place of action → 에서; verb last.
Describing verbs take 이/가, not 을/를.
Everything stacks up in front of the verb.

q: You're leaving; your manager is still working. You say:
why: 수고하세요 = keep up the good work (they stay).

q: Address a manager named 김민수 as:
why: Title + 님, not the name.

q: Politely declining a drink at 회식:
why: Give a reason; 운전 is the universal one.
드시다 replaces 먹다 in honorific speech.
안녕히 주무세요.
Never use 시 about yourself.

q: Most polite way to ask someone to take a photo:
why: 좀 + 주시겠어요 = maximum politeness.
혹시 opens a polite question.
-아/어도 돼요 = may I.
그래서 = so / therefore.
그런데 / 하지만 = but.
Time words set the scene first.
둘 → 두 before a counter; drinks take 잔.
분 is the honorific people counter; 명 is neutral.

q: Where does the number + counter go?
o: after the noun: 맥주 두 병
before the noun: 두 병 맥주
why: Noun → number → counter.

q: Your coworker Minsu, same age. Safe way to address him:
why: Name + 씨 is the polite default with peers.

q: You're a guy; she's two years older. You call her:
why: Male speaker → older girl = 누나.
사장님 = boss/owner, polite and standard.
ㄹ까요 = shall we.
자 = let's.

q: Koreans usually confirm a meetup spot with:
why: e.g. 강남역 11번 출구.
ㅋ = the k in 크크 laughter.
ㅇㅇ = 응응.

q: Texting your older coworker, you should:
why: Shorthand is for friends; politeness stays with seniors.

q: Which vowel is the horizontal 'u' (oo) sound?
why: ㅜ: horizontal stick, tick down = u.

q: What does ㅇ sound like at the START of a block?
why: Initial ㅇ is a placeholder; final ㅇ is ng.
ㅎ + ㅏ + ㄴ (final) = 한.

q: You're ordering at a café. Which form?
why: 요-form is the default with strangers and staff.
반말 = casual speech for close friends and younger people.
-습니다 / -ㅂ니다 is the formal level.

q: 'I'm Lisa' — Lisa ends in a vowel, so:
why: 예요 after a vowel, 이에요 after a consonant.

q: Someone is leaving and you are staying. You say:
why: 가세요 = go well (to the one leaving).
에서 왔어요 = came from.
Money, dates, minutes, phone numbers → Sino.
Hours use native numbers; 셋 → 세 before a counter.
Korean groups by 만 (10,000): 5 × 만 = 오만.

q: To call a waiter you say:
why: 저기요 = excuse me (there). 야 is rude to staff.
Native 둘 → 두 before the counter 개 (things).
먹었 = past (I ate well). 먹겠 = future (I will eat well).
똑바로 = straight.

q: In a taxi, 'please go to Myeongdong' =
why: place + 으로 가 주세요.
T-money works on subway, bus and most taxis.
